newsitem.title: USA: Iraq news depresses U.S. crudes, July grades ease.
newsitem.headline: Iraq news depresses U.S. crudes, July grades ease.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices retreated late Tuesday morning following headline reports that Iraqi oil minister Amir Rasheed expected resumption of Iraqi oil exports in the next week to 10 days.
NYMEX August crude futures topped at $19.45 a barrel earlier in the morning, but worked to lows under $19.00 a barrel after Rasheed's comments hit the wires.

Markets have been hypersensitive to any news on when Iraqi exports would resume under the second round of the U.N. "oil-for-food" accord. Rasheed's comment mirrors statements by senior U.N. officials on Monday. U.N. officials said Baghdad was a week to 10 days from completing an aid distribution plan necessary for restarting the oil sales process.

Cash benchmark August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing tracked around five cents firmer than the NYMEX screen, putting August cash WTI at $19.00-10 a barrel, 15 cents weaker than late Monday. Cash values continued to hold a premium off the Exchange for Physical (EFP) price at plus 4-7 cents.
July/August spreads sold steady from Monday at -28 and -29 cents, putting July WTI/Cushing at $18.70-80 a barrel.

For the grades, refiners were seen mopping up July business ahead of Wednesday pipeline scheduling. Most barrels were selling at weaker price differentials, though volatility in the sweet market kept players jumpy.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 10 cents under WTI/Cushing, down 5-8 cents from Monday. Midland/WTI sold at 26, 25 and 20 cents under July WTI/Cushing.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was steady, attracting deals at 45 cents below marker. West Texas Sour/Midland stayed steady at 75-85 cents under the marker, traders said.
